Finishing Details

Talk through the edges and connections.

The finish includes more than the main paving pattern. Edges, cuts around steps or walls, joints, changes in elevation, and connections between materials all need to be considered. Lighting-ready layouts or sealing coordination can also be discussed when they are relevant to the project.

  • Paver borders, cuts, and edge restraint
  • Joints and transitions between materials
  • Connections around steps and walls
  • Cleanup and discussion of sealing options

A Few Things to Think Through

The edges are part of the design, not an afterthought.

Borders, cuts, joints, and transitions shape how a finished hardscape reads. Reviewing these details alongside the main surface helps keep the pattern and connections consistent across the project.

01

Borders and edges

A border can define the paved area or create a visual frame. Its material and layout should suit the field pattern and edge conditions.

02

Cuts and transitions

Steps, walls, drains, and adjoining surfaces can require careful cuts and changes in material or elevation.

03

Final coordination

Joint finish, cleanup, and any discussion of sealing can be included in the project conversation, depending on the agreed scope.

Questions About Finishing Details

A few useful things to know.

Every property is different. These answers can help you prepare for a conversation about the site and the work.

Can I add a contrasting paver border?

A contrasting border may be an option. The layout depends on the shape of the surface, the field pattern, available materials, and the edges it needs to meet.

Are finishing details part of a larger patio or walkway project?

They can be planned as part of the overall scope. Discuss edges, cuts, joints, and transitions before work begins so they are accounted for in the project.

Do you include sealing?

Sealing needs and options vary by surface and material. Ask the team whether it is suitable and available for the specific project; it should not be assumed as part of every installation.
